dek: Seven Glacier National Park waterfalls with walk lengths, fees and 2026 entry rules. Virginia Falls is the most reviewed; Running Eagle Falls is a 0.3-mile walk.
overview: Glacier National Park is known for melting glaciers, alpine meadows, more than 700 miles of trails and the Going-to-the-Sun Road.

We cover seven waterfalls here. Five are filed under the town of North Browning and two under Columbia Falls, on opposite sides of the park. Virginia Falls has the most visitor reviews, but we don't have a trail length for it. Running Eagle Falls (0.3 mile one way) and Apikuni Falls (0.9 mile one way) are the two with published walks. USGS places Bird Woman Falls on a mountainside, on an unnamed stream about half a mile west-northwest of Mount Oberlin.
fallsIntro: Distances here are one way. Our trail file doesn't say whether you return on the same path, so we haven't doubled them.
plan: The two walks with published lengths are short: Running Eagle Falls at 0.3 mile one way and Apikuni Falls at 0.9 mile one way. Virginia Falls, McDonald Falls, Baring Falls, Redrock Falls and Bird Woman Falls have no mileage in our files, so check trail lengths with the park before you plan a day around them.
flow: The Swiftcurrent Creek gauge at Many Glacier (USGS 05014500) is about a mile from Apikuni Falls. From 2019 through 2024 its average daily flow peaked in June at about 503 cubic feet per second and was lowest in February at about 22.
Glacier's creeks respond to snow and rain at different times in different parts of the park, so treat this as one basin's calendar, not every waterfall's.
feesLead: There is a lower winter rate from November 1 through April 30, and no vehicle reservation is needed in 2026.
access: From November 1 through April 30 the vehicle fee drops from $35 to $25 and the per-person fee from $20 to $15. The park's vehicle-reservation page, updated June 22, 2026, says reservations are not required this year. Logan Pass parking is still time-limited.
safety: The park's weather page says it is generally 10 to 15 degrees cooler at Logan Pass than lower in the park, and that snow can fall in any month. We have no trail-specific warnings on file for these waterfalls, so dress in layers and check conditions before you go.
